title: tanacetum corymbosum
intro: Tanacetum corymbosum, commonly known as tansy, is a perennial plant native to Europe and Asia, characterized by its fern-like foliage and yellow or white flowers. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antispasmodic properties that can help alleviate digestive issues, reduce fever, and ease menstrual cramps. The therapeutic actions of Tanacetum corymbosum include its ability to act as a carminative, an expectorant, and a nervine, making it a potential treatment for various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Tanacetum corymbosum include sesquiterpene lactones, such as thiarubrin and santamarin, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
